What is the recommended way to work with the lattice Set U? The problem is that Set isn't a type class, so I can't write [Set U] in conditions. That's a rather big problem for me. Should I define

class MySet (U: Type*) where
  set: Set U

?

Also, as I remember, there is some construct like [Instance (Set U)] but I can't find it in docs again.
What would you like [Set U] to mean?
@Anatole Dedecker That we use the boolean algebra Set U.

Set U is the type of subsets of U, and it comes with the usual boolean algebra instance, so you can directly use results about the boolean algebra. Maybe it would be easier to help you with an example of what you want to state?

It seems, I understood what to do: I can, apparently, write [BooleanAlgebra (Set α)], instead. I am yet weak in type classes. I understand them partly on example, rather than formally. Maybe, I should read more about type classes.

No, writing [BooleanAlgebra (Set α)] would mean "assume that I am given an arbitrary structure of Boolean algebra on Set α, which might not be the standard one. You shouldn't have anything to write: Lean knows (with the correct imports) that Set α is a boolean algebra for the usual operations.

The problem is that without having the construct [Set U], I need to derive the consequences of Set U having a standard boolean algebra, such as the presence of OrderTop structure, manually. That's very inconvenient.

theorem t1 [t: OrderTop a] : ...  := sorry

theorem t2 (x: Set U) : ... := -- need to invoke `t1 (t := ...)`, what is extremely inconvenient.

I want to deduce OrderTop from x being a set automatically. How?
I think, it is called "type class inference" ("Prolog-like" one, as said in a tutorial). How to use this Prolog-like feature for Set U?

@Aaron Liu I will try to work this out by myself in my (long) code (after having consulted with ChatGPT that steadily says that I don't need [Set U] or its analog). If there will be additional questions, I will.
